title: Could ai revolutonise gaming?
author: Interesting_Fun4411
selftext:
I was thinking, could AI ever reach this level?  
A creative game where people create worldbuilding and maps, and you're just a random guy. There isn't a story to follow—you create it. There are multiple NPCs, maybe legendary swordsmen who lived thousands of years and are very strong with their unique abilities, some randomly generated NPCs, and blah blah.  
You have to train to become strong, and the game generates animations for you. For example, you're training to become a monk with kicks, but unique. It creates the animation, but the model makes it so it's fair: if you actually earned a strong animation with huge damage, it gives it to you. If not, you just get slightly stronger.  
I mean, like, this is the point—listen. The game is a huge sandbox. The game is like Roblox, but on steroids. People type out how the world is: all the places where humans or elves live and stuff. They type the important NPCs—as many as they want—and leave the rest to be randomly generated. Now there would be thousands of worlds and worldbuilding. Maybe in the modern world, maybe fantasy, maybe more. The animations are done on the spot by AI, and you basically create your story. Imagine people could make anything from medieval to modern, to even making, I don't know, even a Breaking bad world in the game with every character.(i know copyrights and all would probably prevent this)  
And this game could be a real-time or turn-based game. A real-time fight would be where you train from before and use animations you set up ahead of time. Let's say the dodging animation you wanted: you make the AI animate it from before and use it so it feels versatile.  
But turn-based, I would argue, is better for fighting in such a game. Let's say he goes to burn you. You can type: "I use a teleportation crystal to go behind him and move my hand horizontally to stab him," and see if it works. Obviously, the AI won't be biased, so it might fail. The good part about this is that you're making a cinematic fight, and the animations are created right in the moment. No pre-made animations—animations created just for that moment. And no, if you try to manifest a god sword or something, the animation will show you trying to, but well, you won't be able to. The enemy AI will look confused and slash you for the mistake.  
But I would think of creating, if possible, one AI for gameplay and monitoring the player so it's fair, and only by training you can get strong (or if the game says you were born OP or you're a genius, but this has to be made at the start of the story—you can't go after starting the game and cheat your way in, you gotta commit).  
Anyways, the second AI will be for the enemies, the NPCs, and worldbuilding and stuff. Why, you may ask? Because if it were all one AI, the enemy AI would know what you would do, so it's just deciding whether it should let it happen or not. I don't like that. So creating a new AI makes it so it has to predict where you will attack, or if you're too slow, it dodges it. This makes the fighting strategic and all.

comments.author: Embarrassed_Split236
comments.body:
Sounds more like a text adventure with AI generated graphics. But I think the core issue with relying on AI to run/make a game is that despite the huge volume and “variety” you could have, it would all be very bland. AI is the definition of quantity over quality, I expect people would much rather play with a carefully crafted and tuned system than one being made up on the spot. 

I think the fluff/visuals/story could be customized by AI, but all the complex bones underneath would probably need human contribution for the balance and game feel to work.

comments.author: SproutsJeremy
comments.body:
In 10 years you will likely be able to type in a prompt and play a AAA game or type in a prompt and play a movie. There will probably also be marketplaces with low cost AAA AI games and AI movies for anyone to play. You will likely be able to choose dialogues, navigate worlds, fight enemies, take on quests. The dialogue will also probably be far less like AI. This is 10 years we’re talking about. 

Will they actually be good? Yeah if you can make your own fun. No if you want something more structured. In other words, regular AAA and indie games will still be far superior over AI AAA games when you’re looking for an custom, tailored, fine tuned experience. 

Imo they will just be separate markets like AI Dungeon is to well written books. Either way, regular game dev isn’t going away soon, but if you’re not being competitive and learning the new AI tools and integrating them into your workflow, you’ll be left behind

replies.author: Kamalen
replies.body:
Everyone keeps saying "what would it be in 10 years" but it’s not even guaranteed it’s going to be that good. The recent releases of frontier models only has marginal improvements and there are signs we may be reaching a diminishing returns phase.

And even if it was truly possible, I don’t see a world where generating an AAA game in real time would be any affordable for the average gamer.
